## Objective

Prove packaged Worker/WASM tick admission and density no-refinement behavior on the supported application paths. #1063 retires the former Reflex-specific auto-attach requirement.

## Acceptance

- Install the packaged Python and Node/browser artifacts and verify the applicable hosted HTML and vanilla TypeScript mounts load their explicit paired tick Worker/WASM assets and display Rust-produced ticks, including applicable secondary/polar paths from #869. Streamlit stock iframe embedding does not advertise automatic Worker URL inference.
- Run with local assets and explicit CSP. No checkout paths, CDN fallback, Node runtime requirement for Python consumption, or hidden asset fetch is accepted.
- In standalone/browser and relevant host-produced exports, deliberately exercise missing/invalid WASM and unsupported refinement sources. Preserve the last valid Rust-authored density overview, expose the documented no-refinement event/reason, and prove no JS aggregation fallback, blank replacement, stale repaint, or leaked worker/resources.
- Distinguish tick setup failures (fail closed per #869) from optional density refinement failure (retain valid overview and report no refinement). Do not blur these contracts.
- Retain screenshots/pixel assertions, events, lifecycle diagnostics, runtime versions, commit and package hashes, and one reproduction command.
- Update the browser-WASM spec and evidence ledger with concrete issue links and supported/fail-closed behavior.

## Relationships and evidence

- Native parent: #40. Final proof depends on #53 packaged browser assets and #869 tick cutover; it blocks #54.
- This is correctness and packaged-integration evidence. Small real-browser cases belong in the applicable existing aggregate; refreshed hosted performance evidence is scheduled/manual and reused from the owning benchmark run.
- No hosted CodSpeed requirement on PRs, no three-identical-run ceremony, and no duplicate full matrix. #54 reuses these cases against final candidate hashes.


## Application host support amendment (#1063)

#1063 removes Reflex support entirely: the adapter namespace, extra, JSX, examples and framework-specific tests retire without a compatibility shim. This amendment supersedes Reflex-specific host/support requirements above. The replacement application consumers are Python/Streamlit and Node/vanilla TypeScript; the shared Python, notebook, HTML/export, native Node, VS Code and direct-browser/WASM surfaces remain.

Use the clean installed consumer gate and coverage disposition in `spec/design/application-consumers.md` and `spec/performance/application-consumers-1063/coverage.md`. Streamlit's stock HTML iframe is a snapshot with browser-local interaction, not proof of Python callback round trips or incremental streaming. Generic channel/widget/Node/browser proofs retain the shared live behavior. Keep packaged Worker/WASM tick admission, strict CSP/offline constraints, missing-asset failure, density no-refinement and resource lifecycle evidence on applicable supported paths.

This support change does not satisfy the remaining GraphForge Streamlit work in #1016, the final candidate matrix in #54, or release qualification by itself. Retain immutable artifact hashes and reuse bounded evidence through the existing Release surfaces gate.
title: Prove packaged WASM ticks and density no-refinement across supported application hosts
